notes: 240 recorded frames after a 60-frame warm-up, on the display's own clock, with at most two frames in flight. The five stages are contiguous timestamps and sum to the reported latency by construction.

Anchored at the moment the frame callback got the CPU, not at link.timestamp: on iPadOS 27 link.timestamp names a vsync still ~3.8 ms in the future when the callback runs, so anchoring there credits the host with time it did not have.

The library's share is 0.87 ms of the 20.44: plan_work 0.012, transaction 0.201, upload 0.065, queue 0.135, GPU execution 0.659. The remaining 19.39 ms is presentation -- one 16.67 ms refresh period on this 60 Hz panel plus the 3.77 ms between the callback waking and the vsync it renders for.

Stable across six consecutive runs: medians 20.44-20.45, zero presentation slip, zero dropped frames. Reaching that needed the host to pace to the drawable. Encoding on every vsync regardless of whether the previous frame had presented let a cold-start backlog sustain itself for a whole run, which measured 50 ms with a 16 ms drawable acquire and 33 ms of slip. That was a host defect, not a library cost, and it is recorded here because the bimodality it produced is the kind of thing a single run would have reported as a library regression.
